transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-05-03 16:00 UTC
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Alex Moreno (Redwood AE), Ravi Patel (Redwood SE), Hannah Lee (CTO, WillowBridge), Marco Silva (ML Engineer), Priya Nair (Infosec)

Summary (auto):
WillowBridge is evaluating Redwood for a hybrid deployment (hosted + potential Private/VPC) to run customer-facing financial chat and document QA. Primary concerns: model choice (open models vs commercial), context window needs (50k ish vs long-doc retrieval), multilingual support for EN/ES/FR, tool-calling for account lookups, and security (KMS, SSO, audit logs). Next steps: pricing, benchmark harness, security docs, and a technical deep-dive on VPC/KMS.

Topics (auto):
- model comparisons (Llama3-like, Mistral, Falcon)
- context length and retrieval + prefix caching
- hosted vs dedicated vs private tradeoffs
- multilingual eval & tokenization concerns
- function/tool-calling patterns (payments/account lookup)
- security: SOC2, KMS, SSO, audit logs

Transcript:
[00:00] Alex (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick voice check and then we'll jump in. I'm Alex, AE. With me is Ravi, our SE. Hannah — can you introduce folks?
[00:12] Hannah (WillowBridge): Yeah hi, Hannah Lee, CTO. Marco's our ML lead, Priya handles security and compliance. We're trying to scope out options for a customer chat + doc QA product.
[00:22] Marco (WillowBridge): Hey all. We ingest bank statements, terms, and chat logs. Latency target is kinda tight for chat — P50 under 200ms ideally, P95 under 800ms.
[00:34] Ravi (Redwood SE): Got it, thanks. Just to set expectations, Redwood supports hosted API, Dedicated reserved capacity, and Private VPC/on-prem. Typical pattern we see is starting hosted for experiments and moving to Dedicated or Private when you need isolation or predictable throughput.
[00:48] Priya (WillowBridge): Right. Our main blocker is security — we need SOC 2, SSO, KMS integration, and audit logs. Also data residency for EU customers.
[00:58] Alex: Totally, we can cover that. Quick question on models — when you say chat + doc QA, are you prioritizing higher accuracy at the cost of latency, or strict latency/cost limits?
[01:12] Marco: Accuracy first for legal/financial answers, but cost matters — we're early stage and can't burn cloud credits. Also, multilingual: English, Spanish and French customer bases.
[01:24] Ravi: OK. For model selection we generally evaluate a couple of open models — Llama-family L3 variants, Mistral-influenced models, and Falcons — and sometimes smaller local models for embeddings/caching. We also look at context-window needs — do you have end-to-end documents longer than the typical 32k?
[01:40] Hannah: Yes, many docs are 40–60k tokens when combined with chat context. We plan to do retrieval augmentation but want larger prefix capacity to reduce retrieval calls.
[01:50] Alex: So two levers: retrieval + embeddings and a runtime with larger context. Redwood supports model variants with different context lengths; we also do prefix KV caching to avoid re-sending repeated system prompt text.
[02:03] Marco: How reliable is the KV cache? Last time we tried something similar in-house, the K V cash had TTL issues and stale caches.
[02:12] Ravi: We call it KV cache but yeah, sometimes speech-to-text. Our runtime manages cache coherence and invalidation policies; you can control TTLs per namespace. Also batching and quantization can be tuned per model.
[02:25] Speaker 3: (mumble)
[02:29] Hannah: On models — do you allow function calling/tool-calling? We need to call internal account lookup service and a payments microservice for specific intents.
[02:38] Ravi: Yes. Redwood supports structured function calling; you can define schemas and we expose streaming responses with tool-calling hooks. For sensitive calls, you can route tool invocation through a private network only on Dedicated/Private deployments. On Hosted we have secure connectors but for complete isolation you want Private.
[02:58] Marco: Are there limitations on streaming when using quantized models? We prefer 8-bit quant to cut cost.
[03:06] Ravi: Quantization interacts with streaming latencies — for most of our supported quant profiles streaming is fine, but very small models or aggressive quant can increase variability. We can run a benchmark with your prompt set.
[03:17] Priya: What about SSO and provisioning? We use SAML and an internal IAM. Also KMS for key rotation — HSM would be preferred.
[03:26] Alex: We integrate with SAML/Okta, SCIM for provisioning, and for Private we support customer-managed KMS and HSM integrations. Hosted supports encrypted-at-rest keys managed by Redwood but can integrate with external KMS for enterprise.
[03:39] Marco: For multilingual, tokenization was a problem with some open models; Spanish gets longer token counts. Any guidance?
[03:48] Ravi: Tokenization varies; we usually recommend model-specific tokenization tests. Some Mistral-ish models are more efficient for multilingual, and we also recommend using embeddings in a separate pipeline so you don't include long context repeatedly.
[04:00] Hannah: We're interested in a hybrid approach: hosted for public-facing lower-sensitivity traffic and Private for EU high-sensitivity accounts. Is that set up possible?
[04:08] Alex: Yes, multi-mode routing is one of Redwood's strengths: policy-based routing by tenant or route, fallback to cheaper models, and per-tenant model pins. You can route EU customers to Private region and others to hosted.
[04:22] Marco: Ok can you do per-route model rollback? We want canary deploys.
[04:27] Ravi: Yes — per-route rollouts, A/B tests, automatic fallback if latency exceeds thresholds. Our Console shows token cost per request and P95 latency traces.
[04:37] Hannah: On cost, what ballpark for a 7B-class open model hosted — tokens per month around 50M? We need a rough monthly burn estimate.
[04:47] Alex: We'll send a pricing sheet. For a quick estimate, a 7B open model on hosted with 50M tokens would be X (we'll put numbers in the sheet), Dedicated tends to reduce per-token cost at commit. Also quantization and caching reduce unit cost.
[04:58] Speaker 2 (Marco): Sorry — X?
[05:01] Alex: Right I said I'll put the exact numbers in an email.
[05:05] Marco: Gotcha. A more technical Q — how do you handle very long retrieval chains? We often do multi-hop where the model needs to reference 10–20 docs.
[05:16] Ravi: Two patterns: 1) retrieve top-k chunks and use a context window + KV cache to keep system-level instructions; 2) use retrieval-augmented generation where we compress retrieved docs with embeddings and summaries so the token input stays manageable. Also Redwood Optimize can suggest chunk sizes and batch configs.
[05:34] Hannah: For evaluation, what should we collect? We can provide sample dialogs and doc pairs.
[05:40] Alex: Perfect — send 3–5 representative threads (sanitized) with target responses and failure cases. We'll run an accuracy and latency sweep across 3 models and return a heatmap.
[05:51] Priya: Security again — audit logs retention and access? We need to show detailed request logs for audits but redact PII.
[05:59] Ravi: Audit logs are configurable. For Private you control retention; we provide immutable audit trail in the control plane for Hosted with export options. PII redaction can be handled via pre-ingest pipelines or runtime redaction hooks.
[06:12] Marco: Anything about on-prem? We do have an internal co-lo for particularly sensitive customers — on-prem deployment for Redwood, how heavy is that?
[06:22] Alex: On-prem is available as a package — requires GPU hosts (we typically recommend A100/H100 class for large contexts) and a private control plane. It's heavier ops but gives full control and is suitable for regulated workloads.
[06:33] Speaker 1 (Hannah): Do you manage model updates?
[06:36] Ravi: We support model pinning; you can pin a model version and roll updates via canary. For open models we curate verified builds and performance profiles. If you want to bring your own model binary, we can onboard it and run validation tests.
[06:49] Marco: Will Redwood help with quantization suggestions? We saw a lot of regressions when aggressive quantization made hallucinations worse.
[06:58] Ravi: Yep — Redwood Optimize includes quantization profiles per model and guidance for tradeoffs. We typically run quality/regression tests against your eval sets before promoting a quantized profile to production.
[07:10] Hannah: One last question on function calling: what happens when tool calls need elevated permissions? For instance, an account lookup needs access to a separate K8s service.
[07:20] Ravi: You can route tool calls through a secure webhook in your VPC; on Dedicated/Private, you can set up an internal-only connector so the model runtime never leaves your network for that call. For Hosted there's a connector with IP allow-listing and mutual TLS.
[07:35] Marco: Great. Could you also show examples of structured responses for downstream parsers? We need deterministic JSON outputs for post-processing.
[07:44] Alex: We have examples and templates; Ravi will include a sample tool-calling schema + examples in the benchmark bundle.
[07:53] (brief chatter)
[08:00] Ravi: Quick architecture sketch: ingest -> embeddings store (FAISS/ann) -> retriever -> Redwood runtime -> function caller. You can use our hosted embeddings or bring your own. For sensitive data, bring your own embeddings and host them in your VPC.
[08:17] Priya: If we bring embeddings in our VPC, does Redwood still see query strings? We need to avoid exposing raw queries.
[08:25] Ravi: For Private you control the entire runtime and embeddings; Redwood control plane only manages metadata if you choose. For Hosted there's an option to use client-side hashing and tokenization to minimize exposure, plus redaction before logs are stored. We'll share the exact flow diagrams.
[08:40] Marco: Any gotchas with multilingual embeddings? We saw cross-lingual retrieval drop for French.
[08:48] Ravi: Use multilingual models for embeddings or language-specific indexes; we can experiment with multilingual vs language-specific embeddings in the benchmark.
[08:58] Alex: Let's talk timeline — are you aiming to pilot in June?
[09:03] Hannah: Ideally early July pilot, yes. Need procurement and security signoff timeline: procurement in mid-late June.
[09:11] Alex: Ok so next week we'll send pricing and the benchmark harness; then schedule the VPC deep-dive with Priya.
[09:20] Marco: For the benchmark, include sample scripts for throughput (QPS) and latencies (P50/P95) and a token-cost calculator.
[09:28] Ravi: We'll include that. Also a small note — if you plan to use long-context L3-like models at 100k tokens, cost scales nonlinearly; often retrieval+compression + KV caching is cheaper.
[09:43] Priya: Do you have a published SOC 2 report?
[09:47] Alex: Yes, we'll attach our SOC 2 and ISO summaries and a short FAQ about KMS/SSO integration.
[09:55] Hannah: Anything else on model selection? We're leaning toward a 13B-class Mistral-ish for accuracy but want a cheaper 7B for low-sensitivity flows.
[10:06] Ravi: That's a common pattern — heavier model for agent-level QA, smaller model for classification/intent + rerank. Redwood routing can do that automatically per intent.
[10:18] Marco: On telemetry, can we export traces to our Datadog?
[10:22] Ravi: Yes, Console supports integrations — Datadog, Prometheus, and you can pull raw traces.
[10:29] (small side conversation)
[10:36] Alex: Ok we'll wrap with concrete next steps — we'll follow up with an email including pricing, benchmark bundle, SOC docs, and a calendar invite for the VPC deep-dive. Any final asks?
[10:48] Priya: Please include details on data residency and how to request EU-only zones.
[10:53] Marco: And sample prompt templates for multilingual QA.
[10:58] Hannah: Thanks everyone. Looking forward.
[11:02] Alex: Great, thanks all.

(End of recording)
